newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS - Market adjusting for rate rise.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS - Market adjusting for rate rise.

text.p: U.S. stocks are pricing-in an interest rate increase and options traders said Monday's intraday lows would likely be a near- to medium-term bottom.

Major index options activity was modest Tuesday but traders said call and put buying had increased recently, indicating investors are positioning for any move in the market after Friday's expiration of March contracts.
"Today is dead quiet," said Jay Shartsis, head of options trading at R.F. Lafferty & Co in New York.
"The market is very hesitant because they're waiting for next week's Fed meeting," he said.
The U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee, which sets interest rate policy, meets next Tuesday.
"They probably will raise rates," Shartsis said. "The market is now adjusting for that, and after they raise rates the market will probably rally."
One index options broker in Chicago said the market's recent pullback had discounted an interest rate increase and that if rates are raised next week, stocks could rally back to record territory.
"I can't see us going down," he said. "Yesterday shocked them. They tried to sell it and couldn't do it."
On Monday, shares fell sharply through most of the day but rebounded in late trading to close moderately higher.
"Yesterday's reversal, taken at face value, was a pretty good reversal," Shartsis said. "Usually you've got to listen to those."
Traders said they expected range trading, with mild options activity, for the balance of the week, with a possible upturn beginning Wedensday if the February U.S. consumer price report is benign.
"I don't think anything tremendous is going to happen this week," Shartsis said.
One index options trader said volume has been relatively light the last few sessions and expected it to remain so through the end of the week, outside of any options-related turnover.
"I haven't seen any big orders," he said. "Volume has been kind of low and I don't anticipate it will pick up."
Among S&P 100 index OEX options, the heaviest volume was in the March 780 calls, which traded 18,130 contracts by about 1240 CST/1840 GMT.
Other busy OEX calls included the March 770, 775 and 800.
On the put side, the most actives were the March 770 and 765, which traded nearly 9,500 and 9,040 contracts, respectively.
The spot OEX was off 2.83 at 769.31.
In the S&P 500, some of the heaviest options volume was in the March and April 800 calls and puts.
The March 800 call traded 4,550 contract, the March 800 put traded 3,430. The April 800 call traded 3,255 and the April 800 put traded 3,400 contracts.
The SPX fell 4.23 to 791.48. June S&P 500 futures were down 4.60 at 799.80.
